keynums.label: PMJDY deposit market share among PSBs

bull_bear.body:
- Capital position remains comfortable with total capital of INR 1,64,696 crore standalone (INR 1,74,989 crore consolidated), CRAR of 16.30% (16.70% consolidated) and CET-1 of 13.90%, alongside a healthy quarterly average LCR of about 127%.
- Book value per share has compounded steadily from INR 197.6 in Q1FY25 to INR 256.2 in Q1FY27 (INR 264.5 excluding the exceptional item), reflecting retention-led capital build rather than external equity.
- Balance sheet is provisioned defensively: provision coverage ratio of 93.28% including technical write-offs (75.07% excluding), and 99.83% coverage on NCLT-referred exposures.
- Capital is raised via layered debt instruments (Basel III Tier II and AT1 bonds rated AAA and AA+ domestically) plus dedicated green instruments, keeping GoI shareholding undiluted at 63.97%.
- Subsidiaries are funded to scale rather than harvested — AMC AUM INR 36,479 crore, IndiaFirst Life AAUM INR 57,210 crore, and BOBCARD active cards at 32.12 lakh with spends up 19.14% YoY.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Total business of INR 30,50,457 crore (global deposits INR 16,33,559 crore, global advances INR 14,16,898 crore), majority owned by the Government of India at 63.97% with FII/FPI at 10.14% and MF/UTI at 9.78%.
- Investment-grade sovereign-linked credit profile: Moody's Baa3/Stable, Fitch BBB-/Stable, S&P BBB/Stable, CARE Edge Global BBB+/Stable, with domestic Tier II bonds rated AAA by CRISIL, ICRA, India Ratings and CARE.
- One of the few Indian PSBs with a material international franchise — international deposits INR 2,52,024 crore and international advances INR 2,65,992 crore, plus wholly/majority-owned banking subsidiaries in Botswana, Kenya and Uganda.
- Deep financial-inclusion moat among PSBs: 14.79% market share of PMJDY accounts and 17.67% share of PMJDY deposits, with 741 lakh financial-inclusion accounts.
- Diversified group structure spanning asset management (Baroda BNP Paribas, 50.1%), life insurance (IndiaFirst, 64.90%), cards (BOBCARD, 100%), broking/IB (BOB Capital Markets, 100%), shared services (Baroda Global Shared Services, 100%), Nainital Bank (98.62%) and India Infradebt (40.99%).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Exceptional Item] Q1FY27 carries an exceptional other-provision of USD 600 million (INR 5,680 crore); the deck presents an alternative 'without exceptional item' view (net profit INR 5,528 crore, RoE 16.57%, RoA 1.10%, BVPS INR 264.5, EPS INR 10.69).
- [NBFC Concentration] NBFC exposure is the largest single industry bucket at 13.2% of domestic advances (INR 1,51,482 crore), though 96.7% of standard NBFC outstanding is rated A and above and 45% is PSU or large-institution backed.
- [Infrastructure De-risking] Infrastructure exposure was cut from 13.1% to 10.1% of domestic advances, driven by sharp reductions in Roads & Ports (INR 33,771 crore to INR 16,358 crore) and Other Infrastructure, while Power exposure grew.
- [Subsidiary Stress] BOBCARD swung to a net loss of INR 103.56 crore in Q1FY27 from a INR 20.80 crore profit a year earlier, and Uganda's subsidiary carries a 13.25% GNPA ratio despite 56.49% profit growth.
- [Employee Welfare] New inclusion-oriented staff schemes introduced — reimbursement of up to INR 20,000 for Smart Vision Glasses for employees with 90%+ blindness, and up to INR 1,000 per dose for cervical cancer (HPV) vaccination for female employees.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Bank of Baroda as a government-majority-owned (GoI 63.97%), AAA-rated large public sector bank with a INR 30.5 lakh crore global balance sheet, a RAM-led (retail-agri-MSME, ~63% of domestic credit) lending mix, a genuinely international franchise, a scaling digital and merchant-acquiring stack, and sector-leading ESG credentials.
